styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a row of four small colour-coded bins with white recycling icons. Measured facts: 12 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage, and 100% of dark edge pixels near-neutral. The tone count is in line with the hedge (9) and below the stall (17) and well (20), so density is acceptable. The outline is the problem. By the numbers it is a neutral black/grey line, and by eye it is a uniform dark frame around every bin. It is not the dark tint of each neighbouring material, which is the Beodeul approach (hedge 0%, stall 1% neutral). Each bin body reads as a flat colour with a lid and a light highlight, so about 3 steps per material against Beodeul's 5-6. There is little grain, dent, rust or per-surface texture. The result looks like a sticker-style icon, shallower than the references, so it fails on outline and shading depth.
